context: Round 61 on run mrun-f77f62158255. Every figure below was read from a live CLI or from disk this session. Four open blocks, each from a real contradiction rather than a preference.

questions.question: The scheduler board and your own ruling now name different next work, and I will not pick silently. bk-flow poll on the glpnet board reports NOTHING DISPATCHABLE, but one packet is state=ready and not_claimed: wp-occurs-checked-substitution-pipeline-compiler-bind-time-occurs-check, which maps to a roadmap feature at WSJF 6.00 / RICE 2000 that already has a spec. Your ruling Q-glpnetshiras-04 (2026-08-30) instead selected front-end-goal-term-acceptance-completeness at WSJF 3.60 / RICE 3000, which is only promoted and still needs /bk-specify. You have also now directed that this lane poll the board and work what the board allocates. Which authority wins when they disagree?
blocks: any board claim from this lane

options.label: Board wins; take occurs-checked
options.means: Claim wp-occurs-checked-substitution on the board and resume it. It is the only READY unclaimed packet, it carries the higher WSJF (6.00 vs 3.60), it already has a spec so the era starts at plan rather than specify, and it is the only choice consistent with your instruction to work what the board allocates.
options.cost: Supersedes your own 2026-08-30 ruling one day later, and the roadmap marks that feature BLK=1, so a blocker must be identified before plan can proceed.

options.label: Ruling wins; take front-end
options.means: Run /bk-specify on front-end-goal-term-acceptance-completeness as ruled, and leave the READY board packet for another lane.
options.cost: Leaves the single dispatchable packet on the board unclaimed while the board reports nothing dispatchable, which is exactly the starvation S16 measured; and starts an era at specify rather than reusing an existing spec.

options.label: Both, board first
options.means: Claim and finish occurs-checked as this era, then /bk-specify the front-end feature as the next era.
options.cost: Two eras committed in advance against a takt band that no era in this repo has yet met; maxi eras currently measure a 22.7h mean against a 1.5-6h band.

questions.question: The tidy-up survey found 8 remote heads not merged into develop. Six are small and mine or shared, but two are large and one is peer-owned. 050-full-gleam-combined is 48 commits ahead and your earlier ruling Q-GLPNETS1-04 already decided '059 survives, archive 050' - so 050 should be archive-tagged then deleted under the provable-containment rule, never merged. 059-full-scope-gleam is 32 commits ahead and maps to a LIVE roadmap feature (specified, WSJF 2.00, BLK 1), so it is feature work rather than tidy-up. chore/host-interconn-hardening-rootcauses-3rtask-olamnit is 1 commit ahead and belongs to the olamnit lane. You asked for the tidy-up branch to be fully complete and merged by the end of this session. How far should this lane go?

options.label: Archive 050 only; leave the rest
options.means: Execute the ruled 050 archive: tag it, VERIFY by ancestry that the tag contains every commit, delete the remote branch. Leave 059 as feature work, and ask olamnit on the channel before touching their head.
options.cost: The repo is not fully tidy at session end - three heads survive - so the goal as you worded it is only partly met.

options.label: Archive 050, merge 083 and 096
options.means: Also merge the two small heads (083 +3, 096 +4) after diffing them, since 096 may already be absorbed into develop and 083 maps to a live WSJF 6.50 feature.
options.cost: 083's work packet is IN-PROGRESS on the board, so merging it may collide with a lane that already holds it; needs a board check first, not just a diff.

options.label: Sweep everything including peers
options.means: Merge or archive all 8 heads this session so the repo ends genuinely tidy.
options.cost: Touches a peer's branch without an ACK, and sweeps 059's 32 commits of feature work through a tidy-up merge - exactly the scope-blurring you told me not to do.

questions.question: buildkit release is blocked on this host by the Claude Code permission classifier - not by any gate, and not something a lane can route around. It blocked me this session with develop 39 ahead of main; a peer lane then cut v2026.08.31.1 and I verified by ancestry that all three of my merged commits reached main, so that instance is discharged. But the block is structural and will recur every time you tell this lane to release. How should this lane handle it going forward?

options.label: Add a permission rule
options.means: You add a Bash permission rule allowing buildkit release in this repo's settings, so the lane can discharge the release half of a ruling without a manual hop.
options.cost: Grants this lane a standing ability to write the release trunk unattended; every future release from here happens without a human in the loop at the moment it is cut.

options.label: Hand releases to a peer lane
options.means: This lane never releases. It merges to develop and states in the coop channel that develop is ready; a peer with an unblocked host cuts the tag, as happened today by accident.
options.cost: Depends on a peer noticing; today it worked only because another lane happened to release for its own reasons, which is luck, not a process.

options.label: Surface it for you each time
options.means: Keep the current behaviour: stop at the block, report it, and print the exact command for you to run.
options.cost: Every release needs you present; the ruling stays half-discharged until you act, and the lane cannot finish an era end-to-end on its own.

questions.question: The reason no era in this repo can be measured is now located, and it is not our code. buildkit_cli.pipeline.schema declares nine ERA_STAGES, but sidecar and controller validate against CANONICAL_STAGES, which holds only six - so codexreview, ship and close can never be recorded. I corroborated this at source on this host after yngwin broadcast it, and it explains the takt output exactly: our era shows all nine steps MISSING and reports unmeasurable, and fleet-wide takt reports 4 eras measured against 68 unmeasurable. The fix is a two-line change in the buildkit lane's shipped code. Your standing instruction is to deliver era and takt metrics into the marathon and then into bk-flow, and that cannot happen until this lands. How should this lane proceed?

options.label: Escalate; do not patch here
options.means: Leave the fix to the buildkit lane as its owner, with the corroboration and the 68-unmeasurable figure already published, and record era-completion as UNMEASURABLE until it lands rather than reporting a six-stage era as if it were nine.
options.cost: No era in this repo can be recorded complete until another lane ships; the takt programme stays blocked on someone else's queue with no ETA.

options.label: Patch locally, upstream after
options.means: Change the two consumers to validate against ERA_STAGES in this host's install, prove eras record end-to-end, and hand the verified patch to the buildkit lane.
options.cost: Forks a shipped fleet artefact on one host - the exact thing that produced three divergent bk-onrestart implementations - and this lane's takt would then differ from every other lane's for a reason invisible in the numbers.

options.label: Take it as a glpnet feature
options.means: Capture it as a roadmap feature here and run it through the full pipeline, since this repo is measurably the worst affected.
options.cost: Claims ownership of buildkit's code from a consumer repo, and duplicates work if the buildkit lane fixes it in parallel - the duplicate-allocation problem you asked me to design out.
